history.answer: My hands have gotten very clumsy and my legs feel stiff and heavy, making it hard to walk.
My hands feel weak and uncoordinated, and my legs feel stiff and heavy rather than just completely numb.
It affects both of my hands and both of my legs fairly equally.
It started very gradually about 6 months ago, and I have not had any sudden weakness.
It has been steadily getting worse over the last 6 months without any relief.
I really struggle with buttoning my shirts, and I keep dropping small tools and screws at work.
My legs feel stiff and uncoordinated when I walk, almost like I am walking on rubber, and I feel unsteady.
Whenever I bend my neck forward to look down, I feel an electric shock shoot straight down my spine.
I have a dull ache in my neck occasionally, but no sharp pains shooting down my arms.
No, my speech is totally fine and my face hasn't drooped at all.
No, I have not had any blurred vision, double vision, or dizziness.
No, I do not have any trouble chewing or swallowing my food.
No, my breathing is completely normal.
No, I have not seen any twitching under my skin, and my muscles have not shrunk.
I have noticed a bit more urgency to pee lately, but I have not had any bowel or bladder accidents.
No, the sensation between my legs and when I wipe is completely normal.
No, I haven't had any fever, cold, or stomach bug recently.
I have high blood pressure, but no history of diabetes, high cholesterol, or heart problems.
I have a couple of beers on weekends, and I eat a normal balanced diet with meat.
No, I have never had any surgeries on my stomach or bowel.
I work with tools as a mechanic, but these clumsy feelings are all over both hands, not just in my wrists.
I take lisinopril 10 milligrams once every morning for my blood pressure.
Just the high blood pressure, which was diagnosed about five years ago.
I have never had any surgery and have never stayed in a hospital.
No, I have no known drug allergies.
No, I have never smoked cigarettes.
I work as an auto mechanic and live in a house with my wife.
My father had high blood pressure, but nobody in my family has had neurologic or muscular problems.
I thought maybe I was just getting older or developing arthritis in my hands and knees.
I am terrified that this will keep worsening until I end up paralyzed and unable to work.
I would like to get a scan of my neck and see a specialist who can help fix this.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 132/84 mmHg, pulse is 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 14 breaths per minute, temperature is 36.7 degrees Celsius, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air.
Cranial nerves II through XII are grossly intact with symmetric facial expression and normal eye movements.
Intrinsic hand muscles show mild bilateral weakness (4/5) with impaired rapid finger tapping, while proximal upper and lower extremity strength is preserved (5/5).
Decreased pinprick sensation over both hands in a non-dermatomal distribution, with reduced vibration sense at the great toes bilaterally.
Brisk hyperreflexia (3+) in biceps, triceps, patellar, and Achilles reflexes bilaterally, with positive Hoffmann signs and positive bilateral Babinski signs.
Passive neck flexion reproduces an electric shock sensation traveling down the spine into the extremities, with no localized spinal tenderness and a negative straight-leg raise.
Gait is stiff, wide-based, and spastic with difficulty performing tandem walking, and the Romberg test is positive.
Full range of motion in all major joints without swelling or deformity, and bilateral Phalen and Tinel signs at the wrists are negative.
